sections.html: The largest and most splendid of all snakeheads belong to the relationship of Channa marulius. This species occurs in India and attains a maximum length of about 120 cm. The largest specimen ever collected is said to have had a length of 183 cm and a weight of 30 kg. But most often the fish become "only" 40-60 cm long. The counterpart of that species in Southeast Asia is Channa marulioides (in fact the specific name means "similar to marulius"). It has now been imported from Thailand. It is likely to have the potential to grow as large as C. marulius, but the largest specimen recorded so far scientifically was only 65 cm long. Currently the fish are 12-15 cm long.
Due to the size, a very large tank is needed, but it is advisable to let the tank grow with the fish. A small fish is easily lost in a too big tank.

These snakeheads are piscivorous. Against other fish that are too large to be eaten, C. marulioides are usually peaceful. The large snakeheads are highly appreciated as food fish in the countries where they occur, but they are also often kept in temple ponds. Here the Channa become very tame, they are fed by the visitors of the temple and they can even be stroked. The elegant predators also become very tame in private aquaria.
